# Wolverhampton Art Gallery

Welcome to Wolverhampton Art Gallery, an urban cultural hub at the heart of the city. Bringing together world-class art, inspiring exhibitions and award-winning creative experiences, the gallery provides opportunities for residents and visitors of all ages to discover, learn, participate and be inspired through creativity and culture.

### Free entry. Everyone welcome!

Welcome to Wolverhampton Art Gallery, a vibrant urban hub for creativity and culture. Founded in 1884, Wolverhampton Art Gallery has stood at the centre of the region’s cultural life for more than a century. Today, it is recognised as a leader in contemporary arts and accessibility, delivering an ambitious and innovative programme of exhibitions, events and projects. 

Home to the largest collection of Pop Art outside London and one of the UK’s most significant collections of work by Black British artists, the gallery connects world class art and creativity with its community of residents and visitors at the heart of the city.

## Getting here

It’s easy to visit Wolverhampton Art Gallery car-free. It is [located in Wolverhampton city-centre](https://w3w.co/vibrates.awards.cost), close to the University of Wolverhampton and St Peter’s Church.

Buses 5, 6 and 876A from [Stafford stop outside](https://bustimes.org/stops/43000702206). Others stop at the university, including services from Cannock. The gallery is also a 5-minute walk from Wolverhampton’s busy bus station.

Metro trams stop at: Wolverhampton, Piper’s Row and St George’s. Each is a 5-minute walk away.

Trains run to Wolverhampton from: Sandwell & Dudley, Stafford, Birmingham New Street, Telford, Stoke-on-Trent and further afield. It’s then a 5-minute walk. On leaving the train station, cross the bridges and continue along Lichfield Street until you reach the gallery.

Wolverhampton is an excellent place to cycle around, with lots of good cycle lanes and a general respect show to cyclists from motorists. There is a secure cycle hub facility at Wolverhampton Interchange where you can store your bike while you explore the city. If you're looking to hire a bike during your time in Wolverhampton, here are the options for [bike hire](https://you-well.co.uk/hiring-bikes/#Wolverhampton/).

We hold the Good Journey Mark for welcoming car-free visitors. Travel a greener way and enjoy 10% off in the cafe. Plan your journey by train, bus, bike or foot at [Good Journey](https://www.goodjourney.org.uk/attractions/wolverhampton-art-gallery/).

## Accessibility

We want to make your visit as enjoyable and straightforward as possible. For information about the accessibility of the venue before you visit, please use our AccessAble Guide for detailed information and images.

- You can borrow noise cancelling headphones from the reception area.
- Please ask if you need a quiet space during your visit or if you need somewhere private to pray.
- There is level access throughout the building and lift access to all floors.
- We have a BSL Introduction to the Art Gallery and you can use the Convo App at our reception desk and pod for live BSL translation.
- We do not have a changing places toilet. The nearest changing place is at the Civic Centre during the week and Wolverhampton train station during the weekend.
- We have free wifi available.
- There is no parking at Wolverhampton Art Gallery. There are accessible parking bays on Wulfruna Street outside the Arena Theatre.

## Family Friendly

We love welcoming families to the gallery, and we are shortlisted for Family Friendly Museum of the Year 2026!

- Explore exciting exhibitions and follow family friendly trails
- Get creative or spend time relaxing together in the Making Space with the art materials, giant chalkboard, art books and Pop Art play area
- Take part in artist-led workshops

- [Visit Family Learning](https://www.wolverhamptonart.org.uk/family-learning)

## Glaze The Eating Space

Glaze The Eating Space at Wolverhampton Art Gallery is our new eating space located on the ground floor. 

A distinctive, historic and stylish look with a modern contemporary vibe that will attract new visitors who will go on to spend time in the art gallery.

The new menu features everything from a Full English Breakfast, Homemade soup of the day, a variety of sandwiches and jacket potatoes (both with different fillings), to our favourite coffees, new loose leaf teas and delicious handmade cakes. 

Whatever time of day your visit there’s certain to be a treat to tempt you.

For bookings, please email [wvcatering.glazecafe@wolverhampton.gov.uk](mailto:wvcatering.glazecafe@wolverhampton.gov.uk) or call [01902 552991](tel:01902 552991).

# Henry Moore Institute

With galleries, an extensive sculpture research library and archive of sculptors papers, visit the Henry Moore Institute to experience, study and enjoy sculpture from around the world.

Find us next door to Leeds Art Gallery in the centre of Leeds, the city where Henry Moore began his training as a sculptor.

 Taking inspiration from bell hooks’ understanding of love as an active and participatory practice, this writing course approaches love as a way of relating to others, to ourselves, to our communities and to the world around us.

 ARTIST PUBLICATION

 Meet art like never before. SoundEscapes is a project connecting art and music and aims to help bring our collection to life.

 New compositions coming soon

 Our new audio tours highlight some of the most unique objects from our global collection. We recognise art as alive and have created two immersive audio experiences to help bring it to life for you.

 Universal Ticket

 ### [Encounter Living Art](https://sainsburymuseum.com/whats-on/living-art/)

 At the Sainsbury Museum and Art Centre, we believe that every artwork has a life of its own. But what does that mean in practice? We invite you to experience the museum as never before.

 16 May - 15 Nov 2026

 ### [What is the Meaning of Life?](https://sainsburymuseum.com/whats-on/what-is-the-meaning-of-life/)

 Universal Ticket

 25 Feb 2027

 Free

 13 Nov 2026 - 30 May 2027

 Our autumn 2026 season explores the profound complexities of human relationships, desire, and intimacy.

 COMING AUTUMN 2026

 ### [Living by the Rule: Contemporary meets Medieval](https://sainsburymuseum.com/whats-on/living-by-the-rule-contemporary-meets-medieval/)

 Exploring the idea of routine and regulation, this exhibition reflected on the ‘rules’ that we live by today, through a dialogue between medieval experiments in a different way to live and modern reflections upon how life is organised.

 PAST EXHIBITIONS

- Past Exhibitions

 ### [Play Power](https://sainsburymuseum.com/whats-on/play-power/)

 Exploring the concept of play in human cultures, Play Power reflected on the broader significance of play and how this is integrated into our daily lives. Would we live a more meaningful life if play were a central focus of day-to-day living?

 PAST EXHIBITIONS

- Past Exhibitions

 ### [Seeds of Hate and Hope](https://sainsburymuseum.com/whats-on/seeds-of-hate-and-hope/)

 This exhibition highlighted personal artistic responses to global atrocities, such as genocides, ethnic cleansing, war crimes and crimes against humanity, challenging the typical representations of war and ‘trauma porn’ often dispelled through the media.

 PAST EXHIBITIONS

- Big Questions Past Exhibitions

 ### [Can We Stop Killing Each Other?](https://sainsburymuseum.com/whats-on/can-we-stop-killing-each-other/)

 This season wrestled with one of the darkest and deadliest aspects of humanity, exploring the fundamental questions of why humans are led to kill and the culture that wrestles with this notion.

 PAST BIG QUESTIONS

- Past Exhibitions

 ### [Roots of Resilience: Tesfaye Urgessa](https://sainsburymuseum.com/whats-on/roots-of-resilience-tesfaye-urgessa/)

 Following a residency with the Sainsbury Centre, internationally acclaimed Ethiopian artist Tesfaye Urgessa unveiled a series of new paintings reflecting on the refugee crisis, which were created in dialogue with the museum’s collection.

 PAST EXHIBITIONS

- Past Exhibitions

 ### [Tiaki Ora ∞ Protecting Life: Anton Forde](https://sainsburymuseum.com/whats-on/tiaki-ora-protecting-life-anton-forde/)

 Anton Forde’s monumental installation of 81 over-life-size figures, Papare Eighty.one (2024) with Shiree Reihana, was shown in the UK for the first time in a new site-specific configuration.

 PAST EXHIBITIONS

 ### [Darwin in Paradise Camp: Yuki Kihara](https://sainsburymuseum.com/whats-on/darwin-in-paradise-camp-yuki-kihara/)

 The UK premiere of 'Paradise Camp', a celebrated work by Yuki Kihara, an interdisciplinary artist of Sāmoan and Japanese descent.

 PAST EXHIBITIONS

- Past Exhibitions

 ### [Sea Inside](https://sainsburymuseum.com/whats-on/sea-inside/)

 Sea Inside turned our oceanic gaze towards the sea’s more intimate spaces – whether physical, psychological or imaginary – and dived into shared watery origins, Indigenous ways of life and the items we remove from the sea to display on land.

 ### [A World of Water](https://sainsburymuseum.com/whats-on/a-world-of-water/)

 What would the world be like without water? This exhibition aimed to unlock a sense of urgency, recognising that water, and possible geopolitical conflicts caused by it, will be as significant in this century as oil was in the 20th.

 ### [The National Gallery Masterpiece Tour: Reflections on Peace](https://sainsburymuseum.com/whats-on/the-national-gallery-masterpiece-tour-reflections-on-peace/)

 The Sainsbury Centre has been selected as a partner for The National Gallery Masterpiece Tour 2025–27. The work selected for the first year was Monet’s The Petit Bras of the Seine at Argenteuil (1872).

 ### [Heroin Falls](https://sainsburymuseum.com/whats-on/heroin-falls/)

 Heroin Falls unflinchingly revealed heroin dependency as seen through the eyes of two remarkable photographers. The exhibition aimed to show how substance use and dependency is a global challenge that transcends race, location and class.

 PAST EXHIBITIONS

- Past Exhibitions

 ### [Ivan Morison: Towards the Weird Heart of Things](https://sainsburymuseum.com/whats-on/ivan-morison-towards-the-weird-heart-of-things/)

 The Sainsbury Centre, in collaboration with Orleans House Gallery, presents Towards the Weird Heart of Things, a new site-specific series of sculptures by artist Ivan Morison in response to the curatorial provocation, Why Do We Take Drugs?

 PAST EXHIBITIONS

- Past Exhibitions

 ### [Power Plants: Intoxicants, Stimulants and Narcotics](https://sainsburymuseum.com/whats-on/power-plants-intoxicants-stimulants-and-narcotics/)

 For millennia people have used the psychoactive properties of plants as an integral part of social, ceremonial and religious life. This show referenced global artefacts that are connected with the traditional consumption of tobacco and snuff, betel nut, kava, tea and palm wine, alongside an exploration of the sacred, hallucinogenic cactus, peyote.

 PAST EXHIBITIONS

- Past Exhibitions

 ### [Ayahuasca & Art of the Amazon](https://sainsburymuseum.com/whats-on/ayahuasca-art-of-the-amazon/)

 This exhibition considered the impact of the mind-altering, psychotropic vine – ayahuasca – within Western Amazonian social life. It explored how the ritual consumption of ayahuasca is linked to their artistic production.

 PAST EXHIBITIONS

- Past Exhibitions

 ### [London Art Fair](https://sainsburymuseum.com/whats-on/london-art-fair/)

 London Art Fair returned to the UK capital from 22-26 January 2025. Sainsbury Centre, the first museum to treat art as a living entity, featured as London Art Fair’s annual Museum Partner.

 PAST EXHIBITIONS

- Past Exhibitions

 ### [Lower Galleries: Tank Man and The Heart of Truth](https://sainsburymuseum.com/whats-on/lower-galleries-displays-tank-man-and-the-heart-of-truth/)

 Two displays in our Lower Galleries. As part of The Camera Never Lies, Tank Man presented photographs and archival video footage from the events in Tiananmen Square on 4 June 1989. The Heart of Truth explored religious teachings of truthfulness within Shinto and Buddhism.

 PAST EXHIBITIONS

- Big Questions Past Exhibitions

 ### [Why Do We Take Drugs?](https://sainsburymuseum.com/whats-on/why-do-we-take-drugs/)

 From alcohol and caffeine to ayahuasca and heroin, this season used art to take visitors on a journey of investigation, inviting audiences to explore the world of global drug cultures from illegal to familiar across one mind-blowing museum landscape.

 PAST BIG QUESTIONS

- Past Exhibitions

 ### [The Camera Never Lies: Challenging images through The Incite Project](https://sainsburymuseum.com/whats-on/the-camera-never-lies-challenging-images-through-the-incite-project/)

 This dynamic exhibition re-evaluated the most iconic images of the past 100 years, exploring the impact and influence photography has had on shaping – and in some cases distorting – the narrative of major global events.

 PAST EXHIBITIONS

- Past Exhibitions

 ### [Jeffrey Gibson: no simple word for time](https://sainsburymuseum.com/whats-on/jeffrey-gibson-no-simple-word-for-time/)

 In his first solo exhibition at a UK museum, American artist Jeffrey Gibson (b.1972) created a new site-specific installation for the Sainsbury Centre.

 Past exhibitions

- Past Exhibitions

 ### [Liquid Gender](https://sainsburymuseum.com/whats-on/liquid-gender/)

 In an exploration of the relationship between gender expression and identity, with a focus on pre-colonial traditions, the Sainsbury Centre presented works by a myriad of internationally acclaimed artists, including new work, UK premieres, and new acquisitions.

 PAST EXHIBITIONS

- Past Exhibitions

 ### [In Event of Moon Disaster](https://sainsburymuseum.com/whats-on/in-event-of-moon-disaster/)

 An Emmy Award-winning interactive experience that was a deep dive into misinformation and conspiracy. Using AI to tell an alternative history, the show brought to light how an event as influential as the 1969 Apollo 11 moon landing could be manipulated, and how doubt could be cast on even the most well-known of facts.

 PAST EXHIBITIONS

- Big Questions Past Exhibitions

 ### [What is Truth?](https://sainsburymuseum.com/whats-on/introducing-our-new-season-what-is-truth/)

 In 2024, the Sainsbury Centre investigated how we can know what is true in the world around us through a series of fascinating, interlinked exhibitions – In Event of Moon Disaster, Liquid Gender, Jeffrey Gibson: no simple word for time and The Camera Never Lies – bringing together some of the world’s leading artists and creative thinkers, plus a new, interlinking publication.

 PAST BIG QUESTIONS

- Past Exhibitions

 ### [Sediment Spirit: The Activation of Art in the Anthropocene](https://sainsburymuseum.com/whats-on/sediment-spirit/)

 Curated by John Kenneth Paranada, the first Curator of Art and Climate Change at a UK museum, this exhibition brought together local and international artworks from the 1960s to the present day that respond to the climate crisis in all its complexities.

 PAST EXHIBITIONS

- Past Exhibitions

 ### [The Stuff of Life | The Life of Stuff](https://sainsburymuseum.com/whats-on/the-stuff-of-life-the-life-of-stuff/)

 In this major international exhibition, visitors met artworks composed of salvaged materials, resynthesised fragments, and e-waste that demonstrate the ingenuity of human creativity to re-imagine our relationships with the planet and inspire people to positively engage with our shared future.

 PAST EXHIBITIONS

- Big Questions Past Exhibitions

 ### [Planet for our Future: How do we adapt to a transforming world?](https://sainsburymuseum.com/whats-on/planet-for-our-future/)

 Our new approach to exhibition programming, empowering art to address fundamental societal challenges through themed seasons, kicked off in Autumn 2023 with Planet for our Future. This asked one fundamental question that confronts us all: How do we adapt to a transforming world?

 PAST BIG QUESTIONS

 ### [Empowering Art: Indigenous Creativity and Activism from North America’s Northwest Coast](https://sainsburymuseum.com/whats-on/empowering-art-indigenous-creativity-and-activism-from-north-americas-northwest-coast/)

 Empowering Art was a ground-breaking exhibition of rich but rarely seen artworks, bringing together exceptional contemporary and historical pieces from across the Northwest Coast of North America.

## Temporary exhibitions

Fifty Years of Change Exhibition

### The Dark Side of Fashion by Michael D Wellington

- 31 October 2026 to 9 January 2027

This photographic exhibition arises out of a project to celebrate gothic metal heads and their unique style. The sitters include both fans and band members who have provided a personal quote on what fashion means to them. The exhibition celebrates the deep connections between music, identity and fashion. These prints will be for sale.

---

### Reflections on a Decade by Bulkington Art Group

- 5 September to 7 November 2026

This group of local artists showcase their work over the last ten years. The work will include landscapes, portraits as well as animals and transport. Some of these works will be for sale.

---

### NEW! Nature in Art

- 14 November 2026 to 27 February 2027

This exhibition brings together two artists whose work is inspired by nature, Katie Fessey and Marisa Sianne.  Their artworks will be complemented by decorative art objects from the museum's collections.
